head: claude/land-9924-attach-target-tests
title: test(ops): land the attach_ib_target coverage from #9924 — the half that never shipped
body:
**This is the disposition of draft PR #9924**, which has sat since 2026-08-18. Tier 1 — one new test file, nothing else. **No `src/`, no `config/`, no order path, no VM.**

Opened via `pr-opener.yml`; this session's GitHub MCP is 403 on writes, so I cannot close #9924 myself — **please close #9924 in favour of this**, or say the word and I will if write access returns.

## Why reduced rather than merged as-is

#9924 changed three files. Two are now redundant, verified by reading `main` rather than by assuming:

| file | disposition |
|---|---|
| `scripts/ops/attach_ib_target.py` | **already on `main`.** The `get_connection` → `trade_journal_db_path()` + `mode=ro` fix is live at `attach_ib_target.py:119`, carrying a comment dated 2026-08-18. It was clearly cherry-picked out so the 07:49Z MGC repair could run. Re-applying it would conflict for no gain. |
| the `BL-20260817-…-UNEXERCISED` backlog row | **duplicate.** `main` already carries `BL-20260818-ATTACH-IB-TARGET-HAS-NEVER-RUN`, filed by whoever landed the hotfix, covering the same defect. |
| `tests/ops/test_attach_ib_target.py` | **absent from `main` — this is the whole remaining value.** |

So the *fix* shipped and the *tests that stop it regressing* were left in a draft for two days. That is the built-halfway-and-left-to-rust pattern, and it is why this is worth landing rather than closing.

## It satisfies a criterion already on `main`

`BL-20260818-ATTACH-IB-TARGET-HAS-NEVER-RUN`'s own resolution criteria say, verbatim:

> *"A regression test that IMPORTS the module and exercises `_open_trade` against a temp DB is required, since a smoke test that never reaches line 102 would have passed this whole time."*

That is exactly `test_open_trade_import_resolves_against_the_real_module` (unstubbed, on purpose — stubbing `_open_trade` is what hid the original defect) and `test_open_trade_opens_the_journal_READ_ONLY` (a temp DB, asserting an `UPDATE` raises so a *repair* tool cannot write the money DB).

## Verified, not assumed

- **8/8 pass against `main`'s already-fixed script** — the point being that dropping the script hunk does not strand the tests.
- **Red-capable, checked by planting the original defect** (`from src.units.db.database import get_connection`): **2** tests fail, not the 1 the PR body claimed — `test_open_trade_import_resolves_against_the_real_module` *and* `test_open_trade_opens_the_journal_READ_ONLY`. Slightly better coverage than advertised. Tree restored and re-verified clean afterwards.
- **`ruff` clean.** Three lint errors in the original file (`S110`, `BLE001`, `UP031`) are fixed here — CI's ruff is diff-scoped, so a new file must be clean. The broad `except` keeps its breadth deliberately, with a `noqa` explaining that narrowing it would couple the test to sqlite's error taxonomy rather than to the defect it pins.

## The one thing NOT carried across, flagged so it is not lost

#9924's backlog row is a duplicate in substance but its **criterion 2 is not** — it generalises the instance into the class:

> *a guard (or registry-test extension) asserting that every action in `EXPECTED_ACTIONS` whose wrapper invokes a python script has at least one test importing that script.*

That is the real fix — *"a registered-but-unexercised script is the same defect as a written-but-never-read provenance field"*, the shape `provenance-consumer-guard` already exists for on the field side. It is deliberately **not** built here (one PR, one concern) and is called out on the coordination board so it does not die with the closed PR.

---

Draft, pending an operator nod to close #9924 alongside it.
